heading: 17.7 Compiler constant-baking must be cross-host deterministic
text:
### 17.7 Compiler constant-baking must be cross-host deterministic [LUNI.17.7]

Pinned normatively in [§2.7]: Rational→`float64` baking
and the tier-2 build-time round-trip test use IEEE 754 `roundTiesToEven` plus a
fixed left-to-right evaluation order, so the same `.ds` yields byte-identical
baked factors on any IEEE-754-compliant build host (DSC reproducibility).

Cross-host conformance vector: the current-state proxy
is `LUNI.2.7_float_repr_roundtrip`, which pins the `FloatLit` source-text →
Python `float()` → `repr()` → lowered-form round-trip for a representative
literal set (a non-binary-representable decimal `0.1`, a small-exponent form
`1e-6`, a full-precision irrational `3.141592653589793`). The chain inherits
IEEE 754 `roundTiesToEven` at parse and produces the shortest round-trippable
decimal at emit, so any IEEE-754-compliant host produces byte-identical
lowered output. The **runtime** serializes a `Float` *value* to JSON in this
same shortest-round-trip form ([LDET.3.2.7]), so a value serialized at runtime
(a cache value, a `call` body) is byte-identical to the same value written as a
source literal here, and round-trips. The full unit-factor-table cross-host vector — bit-comparing
the emitted `.dsc` factor table across architectures — lands with the unit
factor emission slice; a `.dsc` factor table does not exist in the current
emission set.
